title: Unit tests
scope: tests/dfx-protocol.test.js supplies the HTTP answers. Authenticated calls through setup() use DummyAccount unless a test passes another account. Constructions outside setup() pass DummyAccount or no account. Three tests replace the clock with Jest fake timers. tests/package.test.js has no stand-in and checks only the wallet dependency version bound.

entries.mechanism: [ref 0] builds one response object per method and path and passes that function to DfxProtocol as fetch. [ref 1] also replaces globalThis.fetch for the file. In the library, [ref 2] uses the supplied fetch or globalThis.fetch, and [ref 3] sends production calls to https://api.dfx.swiss. The hand-built account and the fixed signature inside [ref 0] have their own entries.
entries.doesNotProve: A green run does not prove that the DFX API accepts these requests or returns these bodies.

entries.mechanism: [ref 0] is the default account address, 20 bytes ending in 1, and [ref 1] makes getAddress return it. It is not the address of the public test key used elsewhere in the file. [ref 2] uses the 40-hex string 0xabcdef…abcd, which has the shape of an EOA, as the account address for a matching-case buy or sell. The Tron label on the next line does not have that shape. [ref 3] uses the same 40-hex string as the account address when a challenge differs only by case.
entries.insteadOf: the address of the account's key
entries.doesNotProve: A green run does not prove that this address belongs to a key or that a chain recognizes it.

entries.mechanism: [ref 0] installs Jest fake timers around a country read and expects no timer to remain. [ref 1] and [ref 2] install Jest fake timers and replace setTimeout with a spy that calls the fake setTimeout captured after that installation. Those tests advance that clock to the configured deadline and expect the request to abort then. [ref 3] restores the real timers after every test.
entries.doesNotProve: A green run does not prove that these requests abort after the same delay on a real clock.
